issues.detail: The Hebrew 'שָׂרוֹת' (śārôt) means 'princesses' or 'noble women' (plural of 'שָׂרָה'), not a proper name '撒拉' (Sarah). The Chinese renders it as a transliteration of the personal name Sarah, which would mislead a reader into thinking these were women named Sarah, whereas the Hebrew refers to their status as princesses/noblewomen.
